story: At 12:17 on a sunny Monday in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Donna stand on Magnolia Loop making plans with Rosa for a Tuesday evening on her porch, where Gary will bring wiring sketches and Donna will bring cart ideas that still have to clear Architectural Review. Donna also reminds Gary to choose a day this week for the court, since she booked just two hours. Rosa, upbeat as ever, thanks Gary for filing first and asks for a removable red cross glow and slow heartbeat blink on the hospital cart, something that won't count as a permanent modification until Review approves it. Hal, watchful as always, has just headed toward his house, keeping an eye on the street as the others keep their plans moving.
events: Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Donna offered pickleball court time and wants to sketch cart plans after; Rosa offered Tuesday/Thursday evenings at her porch at six. I've already pitched my wiring sketches and filed with Architectural Review, so no need to repeat myself. What's useful now is answering their actual offers: lock in Rosa's porch at six, bring sketches that pass review, and give Donna a concrete day for the court. Staying useful and needed is what I'm about, and a clear answer keeps the parade moving.

parameters.content: Tuesday at six on your porch works for me, Rosa. I'll bring the wiring sketches, nothing that'd bother Architectural Review. Donna, I'm free Wednesday for that court, and I'll try not to embarrass myself.

donna.thought_process: Rosa has offered Tuesday and Thursday evenings at six on her porch for parade planning, and Gary is waiting on a pickleball time. I already pitched the court once, so I shouldn't repeat myself. Best move is to answer Rosa's actual offer, lock in Tuesday at six, commit to cart ideas that pass Architectural Review, and pin Gary down with a pickleball slot while we're all here. That keeps things moving and within the rules.

parameters.content: Tuesday at six on your porch, Rosa, you're a doll. I'll bring cart ideas that go through Architectural Review first, and Gary, bring those wiring sketches. And Gary, pick a day this week for the court, I booked two hours, and that's all L-05 lets us have!

hal.thought_process: Baseline is logged, binoculars swept twice, and nothing's changed on the Loop. Halloween decorations are welcome all week, so the real inspections come later. My goal is to report Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos to the committee, and I can't file anything without a documented violation. No sense burning daylight on the porch. Best use of this hour is to walk the Loop and eyeball things up close, since binoculars only show so much and a notebook entry needs a firsthand count. Order and respect, and that means evidence.

parameters.content: Walking the Loop to check cart mods and ornament counts up close before Halloween decorations go up

rosa.thought_process: Gary asked what my hospital theme needs from the lights, and Donna is mid-plan with him about courts and cart sketches. I haven't answered Gary yet, and my memories show I already proposed Tuesday/Thursday evenings on my porch, so I shouldn't repeat that. Best move is to answer Gary's actual question concretely: a hospital theme needs a soft red cross glow and a heartbeat-style blinking, nothing that's a visible exterior modification until Review signs off. That moves the parade plan forward and keeps everyone friendly and within L-01.

parameters.content: Gary, thanks for filing first, that's how we keep Hal off our backs. For the hospital cart I'd love a soft red cross glow and a slow heartbeat blink, battery LEDs I can clip on and take off so nothing counts as a permanent mod until Review says go.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
